# FG-GIT-0032

| 項目 | 値 |
|---|---|
| HTTP ステータス | 500 |
| 重大度 | warn |
| Runbook | なし |
| 発生させるテスト | `a_batch_process_that_dies_mid_answer_falls_back` |

## 利用者向けメッセージ

- ja: リポジトリの読み取りで一時的な問題が発生しました。問い合わせ番号を添えて管理者に連絡してください。
- en: A temporary problem occurred while reading the repository. Contact the administrator with the request ID.
- id: Terjadi masalah sementara saat membaca repositori. Hubungi administrator dengan menyertakan ID permintaan.

## 原因 (cause)

The browse API reads objects (trees, blobs, commit headers) through a long-lived `git cat-file --batch-command --buffer` process per repository (forge_git::batch: at most `BrowseLimits::batch_per_repo` (2) per repository, `batch_max_repos` (32) repositories, closed after `batch_idle` (60 s) unused). One exchange with such a process failed: it could not be started, it exited or closed its output in the middle of an answer (`reason=io`, with `source`), it answered out of protocol (`reason=protocol`: a header that does not name the requested object, a size that does not match, a missing trailing newline), or it did not answer within `batch_timeout` (2 s, never past the browse deadline; `reason=timeout`). The process is killed and never reused, and the same read is answered by the one-shot git command (`ls-tree`, `cat-file blob`, `cat-file --batch-check`) — the user gets the normal answer (or that command's own error); this code is never returned to a user.

## 調べ方 (diagnosis)

One warn event `forge.git.batch.fallback` per failed exchange with `error_code`, `reason`, `op` (`info` / `contents`), `repo_id` and the request's `request_id` span. Isolated events: a git killed from outside or a slow disk. Many for one repository: run `git -C <path from forge admin repo-path> fsck --connectivity-only` (a corrupt object makes cat-file die) and compare with FG-GIT-0003 events of the fallback. Other reasons, each said once: `reason=unsupported` (event `forge.git.batch.unsupported`, with `git_bin`): the first process exited with git's usage status 129 — this git has no `--batch-command` (< 2.36, below forge's minimum 2.38: `git.bin` points at another git); the pool turned itself off and every read is a one-shot git until the restart. `reason=release_timeout` (event `forge.git.batch.release_timeout`, `repo_id`, `timeout_ms`): before a purge, a gc or a restore, a batch process of the repository in this process did not exit within 5 s; the step goes on and reports a file still in use itself. `reason=files_in_use` (event `forge.git.maintenance.files_in_use`, `step=gc`, `repo_id`, `retried`, git's `stderr`): gc could not delete an old pack because another process holds it (a `forge serve` batch process on a git without delete sharing); gc ran once more after 95 s when the job's time allowed (`retried`); the pack left behind is removed by the next gc. The debug event `forge.git.spawn` (target `forge_git::spawn`, `kind=batch`) counts the processes started.

## 対処 (fix)

Nothing to do for isolated events (the read was answered by the fallback). For a corrupt repository follow runbook repo-maintenance (fsck → FG-GIT-0019). If the events persist, the long-lived processes can be turned off by setting `BrowseLimits::batch_per_repo` to 0 (every read is then a one-shot git, ~20–40 ms more per read on Windows).
